projects.title: The Univer-City
projects.description: The university is a melting pot of different sciences and forms of knowledge. It is an alternative discipline that indirectly supports our society. The idea of the univer-city aims to break the imaginary frontier between these two entities, turning the university into an open space with multiple sources of exchange. In our vision of the territory, it makes sense to see Brussels as a complex web in which the univer-cities play an important role. The Solbosch pole plays its part in this network. We highlighted five main aspects of the Solbosch campus and its surroundings at the scale of the Brussels University District. Connecting the campus to the city, mobility systems, landscape design, environmental development, including water management and energy, and the notion of harmonism in broader terms are the main points of concern. These strategies help us discuss sustainability beyond environmental issues, while also taking the social and economic dimensions into account. By connecting the university with the city of Brussels, the campus can be transformed into an open space for the neighborhood. Our first ambition is to open the campus to the city. In that regard, we provide several shared areas such as swimming facilities, sports fields, urban farming, a rooftop playground, open libraries, a café and food services, a ressourcery, auditoriums, and multifunctional spaces for public events, conferences, and more. Therefore, the new entrance building is conceived as a link to the city, filled with community services. We then focus on mobility at the scale of the campus and the BUD.
projects.client: Yasmin Allaouzi, Niloofar Amini, Paulien Beeckman, Pauline Harou, Ahmed Soliman, and Alexandre Rovere

projects.title: Leap of Faith Bridge
projects.description: We won second place in the FEDA Week 13 Students’ National Competition 2012/13 on the theme of Bridge of the Future. Competing against more than 60 other universities, our project was designed to provide responsive movement that varies according to different conditions. The bridge represents the leap of faith people must take to move from their past into the future. A glass section in the middle forms an obstacle symbolizing the challenges people face in life. Users must choose to step forward and take that leap into the future.
projects.client: Mohamed Mahmoud, Mazen Nabil, Fatma Abd Elrahman, Abdullah Gabr, Ayman Shawki, Mostfafa Elsayed, Haytham Kamal, Ahmed Soliman

projects.title: Bending-active responsive grid shell
projects.description:
This project explores the combination of bending-active structural elements within a responsive system. The pavilion consists of a grid shell that can be controlled by a set of wires. These wires can be tensioned separately by users according to different needs and weather conditions. The aim of the project is to strengthen the connection between Brussels residents and outdoor space, while giving users the opportunity to alter and shape the pavilion. The seven tensioned wires generate dozens of possible configurations. 

Temporary structures are everywhere. They define outdoor spaces and fill the void between permanent constructions. They follow the organic evolution of cities’ needs and daily functions. Such organic development should be supported by transformable systems that provide flexibility. Transformable structural systems can shift from one state to another. They can be rapidly assembled and disassembled, then transported elsewhere to reuse the same materials and reduce waste.
projects.role: Design, Research, structural analysis, parametric modeling

projects.title: The Chavilion: Scissor chair-pavilion
projects.description:
The Chavilion is a design project for an indoor pavilion created for the architectural atelier at VUB. The pavilion is a kit-of-parts system composed of a main repetitive unit. The system is intended to function like Lego, ensuring transformability. The main element is a stand-alone functional chair with scissor deployability. Connecting six to eight chairs together creates the arch of the pavilion, which remains deployable. 

The project included a structural analysis using the “Karamba3D” plugin in Grasshopper. It also involved creating a 1:5 scale scissor system to test the overall functionality of the project. The chair uses the scissor mechanism to provide five different modes of use.
projects.role: Conceptualization, Design, Research, structural analysis, parametric modeling
projects.client: Ahmed Soliman, Hana Taherazar, Pauline Harou, Razan Atwi.

projects.title: ULB Timber Tower: Timber Is the New Concrete
projects.description: The ULB Timber Tower is part of a master plan to develop the ULB campus in Brussels, Belgium. The project proposes an entrance building that directly welcomes visitors and students arriving along the campus's main axis. The aims of the ULB Timber Tower reflect the vision of the master plan while pursuing four main goals: 1) to promote sustainability and lead the community by example; 2) to establish a symbolic identity for the university; 3) to strengthen the connection between the city and the university; and 4) to provide the functional spaces needed to accommodate the constant increase in students and expand university capacity.
projects.role: Conceptualization, Design, Research, Structural Analysis, Environmental Analysis, Parametric Modeling

projects.title: Konligo: Internship – Research and Development
projects.description: Konligo is a Belgian start-up specialized in lightweight and transformable structures. Its mission is to push temporary structures to the next level while helping the event industry move toward a more sustainable future. I joined the R&D team and participated in developing deployable scissor-structure technology. During my internship at Konligo, I had the chance to work across several departments. One of the benefits of working in a relatively small team is the opportunity to be involved in many different fields and gain a broader understanding of how everything works. I was trained as an engineer, but I also developed strong entrepreneurial skills.
projects.role: R&D, Research, Parametric Modeling, Computational Production, Graphic Design, Video Editing. The structure was originally designed by the Konligo team.

projects.title: Prison de Saint-Gilles: 2030
projects.description:
The prisons of Saint-Gilles have been emptied, leaving an exceptional site of more than 10 hectares to be rehabilitated near the center of Brussels. We developed a full plan to transform the prison buildings into a multifunctional project that liberates the land and gives the site back to the city. The project won first place in the “Design Project Competition” course, taught by Vincent Gérin and judged by jury members Luc Deleuze, Laurent Vrijdaghs, Vincent Wathelet, John Pitseys, and Françoise Sacchi. 

I also had the opportunity to share the stage at the “Realty Belgium Real Estate Summit” with Benoit Moritz, Laurent Vrijdaghs, and Vincent Gérin as part of a discussion on case studies related to the reconversion of Saint-Gilles Prison in September 2022.
projects.role: Design, Research, Financial plans, conceptualization, computational production, rendering.

projects.title: Bending-active plate components in configurable kit-of-parts systems
projects.description: This research investigates transformable wooden kit-of-parts systems through digital and physical modeling. It conceptualizes the structure as an assembly of modular components constructed on site and proposes a reconfigurable temporary system capable of adapting to different shapes and sizes using a consistent set of elements. A systematic method for connecting components is introduced, based on joints arranged within symmetrical grids and solids. Each face is replaced by a modular element, with pairs of elements connected through a single joint. The resulting structural configurations are derived from thoroughly studied polyhedral geometries or tessellations. The regularity of these systems is key to their reconfigurability.

projects.title: First permanent moon base
projects.description:
The spacefaring age promises immense potential, offering humanity access to vast resources, materials, and energy beyond Earth. In 2004, George W. Bush introduced a vision for renewed lunar exploration through a series of robotic missions designed to gather data on lunar resources and identify suitable construction sites for future habitation.

This project presents a vision, conceived in 2014, of an early step toward the colonization of the Moon. It explores the development of an initial unmanned lunar base as the foundation for a permanent human presence.

The first permanent Moon base represents a critical milestone in the transition to a new era of exploration. It will enable deeper access to the solar system, support the establishment of extraterrestrial settlements, and shift humanity’s perspective from a “closed Earth” mindset to a broader, open-space vision of progress and discovery.

projects.title: The Barber
projects.description:
An interior design project for “The Barbershop,” a growing chain of barbershops based in Egypt. Designed and implemented in 2020, the project was developed by Soliman in collaboration with co-designer Aacer El Noshokaty, working as freelance architects.

The project encompassed the full interior design process, from concept development to detailed execution drawings, with a focus on creating a distinctive and contemporary spatial identity. The design aimed to reinterpret the traditional barbershop experience through a modern lens, balancing functionality, comfort, and a strong visual character.

In parallel, the scope included the development of a complete brand identity, covering logo design, visual language, and overall branding strategy to ensure coherence between the physical space and the brand’s image.

The shop is currently operational in Cairo.
projects.role: Interior design, rendering, modeling, lighting, logo design, identity design, supervision of implementation.

projects.title: ReciPlyDome
projects.description:
In the event sector, where there is a growing demand for architectural structures with innovative morphology, reuse is essential for achieving more sustainable events. Designing modular structures and detailing them for easy disassembly and reassembly is an ideal way to encourage and facilitate reuse. In this way, a longer lifespan can be ensured for the components used. However, temporary event structures are often difficult to assemble, which can compromise their reusability. These assembly challenges are usually caused by the morphology of the modules or by the types of connections used. Therefore, such structures require optimization in terms of assembly while remaining resource-efficient.

The main objective of this research is to reimagine the ReciPlyDome and optimize it in terms of assembly. The ReciPlyDome is a reciprocal dome structure based on a rhombic triacontahedron, in which all elements are identical except for the five elements that touch the ground. During the assembly phase of the first version of the ReciPlyDome, torsion in the components appeared to hinder efficient construction. To eliminate this, the dome was reviewed, which led to the development of a new connection system and an improved beam geometry. A new full-scale version of the dome was then built, demonstrating the positive effect of the improved connector system and the optimized beam position. In situ measurements were taken after construction, showing good correspondence between the digital and built models. Further research will focus on developing a covering system for this modular reciprocal dome for outdoor use.
projects.role: Technical optimisation, modeling, cover design, research, construction.

projects.title: Integration of rigid plates in deployable scissor structures
projects.description: This research investigates two geometric approaches for integrating rigid plates into deployable scissor structures, aiming to overcome the limitations of flexible membrane coverings in temporary architectural applications. Scissor grids are well known for their rapid deployability and compact storage, yet their broader application has been constrained by coverings that contribute little to structural capacity and often lack durability. To address this limitation, two novel strategies are proposed in this research: (i) extrusion-surfaced plates embedded within uniaxially transforming planar scissor structures, and (ii) hyperbolic ruled surface plates incorporated into three-dimensional scissor modules. The study combines the automation process of geometric modeling, deployment constraint analysis, and joint optimization to examine the feasibility and implications of these hybrid systems. Results indicate that rigid plate integration expands the range of spatial configurations achievable with scissor grids and improves their functional potential. By advancing design methodologies for hybrid deployable systems, this work contributes to the development of more robust, reconfigurable, and efficient solutions for temporary spatial applications.
projects.subtitle: geometrical modelling and design by prototyping

projects.title: Freelance Projects (2013–2019)
projects.description:
This page presents a curated selection of freelance work developed between 2013 and 2019, spanning a wide range of design services across architecture and visualization.

During this period, I worked independently on diverse projects that included architectural design, 3D rendering, and the development of execution drawings, as well as oversight of renovation works. The scope of work also extended to façade and elevation design, alongside various design outputs and technical consultations tailored to client needs.

These projects combine conceptual thinking with precise technical development. Visualizations were primarily produced using 3ds Max and V-Ray, enabling detailed and realistic representations that supported both the design process and effective client communication.
projects.subtitle: Location: Egypt

projects.title: 3D Car Modeling from Scratch
projects.description: This project explores the complete process of building a 3D car model from the ground up using 3ds Max, without relying on any imported geometry. The model was developed through a polygonal modeling workflow, starting from simple primitives and progressively refined to achieve accurate proportions. The final model was then prepared and optimized for rendering using the Mental Ray engine. In addition, AI-based rendering tools (Nano Banana 2) were used to further refine and validate the visual concept, supporting a more realistic proof of concept and enhancing the overall presentation quality.

projects.title: Origami villa
projects.description: This project presents a conceptual villa design that explores architectural form through the lens of origami-inspired folding. The design focuses on translating folded geometries into spatial compositions, where surfaces and volumes emerge from continuous, dynamic transformations.
